fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled input bytes are parsed as a 16-bit length prefix; this chunk length determines how many bytes are returned as the next APDU response.
The last two bytes of each fuzzed chunk become the APDU status word, letting the attacker control whether Coolkey match_card and subsequent APDUs succeed.

fine_trace.code: r = sc_transmit_apdu(card, &apdu); if (r == SC_SUCCESS && apdu.sw1 == 0x6d && apdu.sw2 == 0x00) return 1;
fine_trace.note: Attacker makes the GET_STATUS APDU return 0x6D00 so the Coolkey driver is selected.
Allocates coolkey_private_data_t and initializes objects_list with copy_data=1 and coolkey_list_meter as the element size function.

fine_trace.code: r = coolkey_read_object(card, COOLKEY_COMBINED_OBJECT_ID, 0, object, object_len, priv->nonce, sizeof(priv->nonce));
fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled APDU response supplies the combined-object bytes that will be parsed by coolkey_process_combined_object.

Each sub-object parsed from the combined object is copied into a freshly malloc'd buffer and appended to priv->objects_list; the list stores a shallow copy of the struct, so the data pointer is shared with the stack copy.
list_append copies the sc_cardctl_coolkey_object_t struct (including the data pointer) into the list; the malloc'd buffer is now owned by the list entry.
If any later step in coolkey_initialize fails (e.g. the object list loop returns an error), cleanup frees every o->data in the list, frees token_name, and frees priv itself.
When sc_disconnect_card is later invoked, coolkey_finish reads card->drv_data and calls coolkey_free_private_data again on the same (already freed) priv, causing the heap double-free.
